categories.note: Silhouettes show the kind of ship (fleet submarine, destroyer, escort, auxiliary gunboat, merchant ship, tanker, fighter aircraft), not each one's own outline, and are not to scale.

corsair.name: F4U CORSAIR
corsair.type: Vought F4U, Navy and Marine fighter
corsair.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), F4U plate

dinah.name: DINAH 43
dinah.note: The plate is headed DINAH 3; the July 1945 revision renames it DINAH 43. Pages 43-44 are the revision's own numbering; HyperWar's markers number them 45-46. The DINAH 2 plate is not among the revised pages, and the records do not say which model the CAP splashed on 6 April 1945.

ju88.name: JU 88
ju88.type: Junkers Ju 88A-6 (plate for the Ju 88 series), medium bomber-fighter
ju88.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), Ju 88A-6 plate, leaf n118
ju88.note: The plate is the Ju 88A-6 ("Ju. 88 series"); FM 30-30 has no separate A-4 plate.

beaufighter.name: BEAUFIGHTER
beaufighter.type: Bristol Beaufighter I (plate for Marks I, II, VI), fighter
beaufighter.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), Beaufighter I plate, leaf n92
beaufighter.note: The plate is the Mark I and covers Marks I, II and VI; it does not show a Mark VI night fighter's radar aerials. The head-on view's gaps between nacelles, fuselage and tailplane are closed (traced from the plate closed by 10 px), so it is blockier than the plate.

fw200.name: FW 200
fw200.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), F.W. 200K plate, leaf n132

z1007.name: Z.1007
z1007.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), CANT. Z-1007 bis plate, leaf n180

he111.name: HE 111
he111.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), He. 111K plate, leaf n120

bf109.name: ME 109
bf109.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), Me. 109F plate, leaf n110

fw190.name: FW 190
fw190.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), F.W. 190A-3 plate, leaf n112

p47.name: P-47 THUNDERBOLT
p47.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), P-47D plate, leaf n26

p51.name: P-51 MUSTANG
p51.type: North American P-51 (P-51 series, A-36; RAF Mustang I), fighter
p51.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), P-51 plate, leaf n28
p51.note: The plate is the Allison-engined P-51/A-36/Mustang I, not the P-51B/D.

p39.name: P-39 AIRACOBRA
p39.type: Bell P-39E (P-39 series; RAF Airacobra I), fighter
p39.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), P-39E plate, leaf n22

hurricane.name: HURRICANE
hurricane.type: Hawker Hurricane IIc (Hurricane I, II), fighter-light bomber
hurricane.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), Hurricane IIc plate, leaf n80

hudson.name: HUDSON
hudson.type: Lockheed A-29 Hudson (RAF Hudson I to VI), light bomber
hudson.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), A-29 plate, leaf n34

spitfire.name: SPITFIRE
spitfire.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), Spitfire V plate, leaf n78

wellington.name: WELLINGTON
wellington.source: FM 30-30 Recognition Pictorial Manual (April 1943), Wellington IV plate, leaf n84
wellington.note: The plate prints the length of the Mark II (61 ft) and Mark III (61 ft 6 in), not the IV; 61 ft is used.

p108.name: P.108B
p108.type: Piaggio P.108B, four-engined long-range bomber (Regia Aeronautica, 274ª Squadriglia BGR)
p108.source: Not a wartime plate: traced from a modern three-view, Kaboldy, "Piaggio P.108.svg" (Wikimedia Commons, 2013), CC BY-SA 3.0. Span and length (second series) from Ali e Uomini, Piaggio P.108B
p108.licence: CC BY-SA 3.0 (this entry only, as an adaptation of the Commons drawing; attribution: Kaboldy, Wikimedia Commons)

sumner.name: SUMNER class DD
sumner.plate: ONI 54-D, 22 Jan 1944: bow 20', stern 10', bridge 35', stack 46', mast 84', length 376'

essex.name: ESSEX class CV
essex.plate: ONI 54-CV, Nov 1943: deck 57', bridge 93', stack 113', mast 147'

independence.name: INDEPENDENCE class CVL
independence.plate: ONI 54-CV: deck 46', bridge 68', stack 58', mast 117', length 610'

cleveland.name: CLEVELAND class CL
cleveland.plate: ONI 54-C, Nov 1943: bow 27', stern 22', bridge 59', stack 77', mast 113', length 610'

gato.name: GATO class SS
gato.plate: ONI 222-US, 1 Sep 1945, p. 113: length 311'9", beam 27', draft 16'8" max. The plate prints no heights, so the outline is traced from its profile and scaled to the printed length

balao.name: BALAO class SS
balao.plate: ONI 222-US, 1 Sep 1945, p. 109: length 311'6", beam 27'4", draft 16'9". The plate prints no heights, so the outline is traced from its profile and scaled to the printed length

fletcher.name: FLETCHER class DD
fletcher.plate: ONI 222-US, 1 Sep 1945, p. 89: length 376' (oa), beam 40', draft 15' max; the plate's own 0-90 ft scale reads the mast at 75'. Traced from its profile and scaled to the printed length (the scale and the plate agree to within a few feet)

buckley.name: BUCKLEY class DE
buckley.plate: ONI 222-US, 1 Sep 1945, p. 117: length 305'11" (oa), beam 36'10", draft 10'9" max; the plate's own 0-90 ft scale marks the mast yard at 75'. Traced from its profile (the turbo-electric units' trunked stack) and scaled to the printed length; the scale reads about 3% longer

lst1.name: LST (Landing Ship, Tank)
lst1.plate: ONI 226, Allied Landing Craft and Ships, 7 Apr 1944, p. 110: length 328'0" (oa), beam 50'0"; sea-going draft 8' fwd, 14'4" aft. The plate's inboard profile is a line drawing with no printed heights: its outline traced with the outside flooded, scaled to the printed length, and cut at the sea-going waterline (the heights are the drawing's, at that scale: the mast about 74 ft). The 2-davit ships, without an LCT on deck

argentina.name: ARGENTINA, BRAZIL, URUGUAY (liners)
argentina.plate: ONI 208, Merchant Ship Recognition Manual, 21 Apr 1942, p. 13 (profile "Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay", turbo-electric, 1929, 20,614 GT; index p. 51). The plate prints no dimensions, only a 0-500 ft scale bar: the outline is traced from the profile (rigging dropped, masts drawn back at the plate's positions and heights) and measured on that scale, 590 ft (Wikipedia gives 613 ft overall). Mirrored to put the bow on the right

ancon.name: ANCON, CRISTOBAL, PANAMA (Panama Railroad liners)
ancon.plate: ONI 208, Merchant Ship Recognition Manual, 21 Apr 1942, p. 27 (profile "Ancon, Cristobal, Panama", printed sideways; 1939, 10,021 GT; index p. 50). The plate prints no dimensions, only a 0-500 ft scale bar: the outline is traced from the profile (cargo booms and stays dropped, masts and kingposts drawn back at the plate's positions and heights) and measured on that scale, 511 ft (Wikipedia gives 493 ft). As a merchant liner, before her 1942-43 conversions. Mirrored to put the bow on the right

shimushu.name: SHIMUSHU class PF (Etorofu type kaibokan)
shimushu.plate: ONI 222-J, The Japanese Navy, issued June 1945, p. 107 (scan leaf 130): length 255' 0" (oa), 245' 0" (pp), beam 30' 0", draft 9' 0" (mean); the plate's own 0-75 ft scale marks the mast yard (dotted line) at about 62'. Lists SHIMUSHU, KUNAJIRI, HACHIJO, ETOROFU, OKI, TSUSHIMA, FUKUE, AMAKUSA, MANJU, KANJU, KASADO (*UKURU, *OKINAWA, *AMAMI, *AGUNI now listed under UKURU class). Traced from its profile (shaded line drawing, threshold 205, gun barrels and wires dropped) and scaled to the printed length; the scale reads the foremast top about 68', the trace 69'

mikura.name: MIKURA class PF (Mikura type kaibokan)
mikura.plate: ONI 222-J, issued June 1945, p. 109 (scan leaf 132): length 275' 0" (oa), beam 35' 0", draft not printed; 0-90 ft scale, dotted line at about 66'. Lists MIKURA, MIYAKE, NOMI, KURABASHI [sic, KURAHASHI], YASHIRO, CHIBURI, SHONAN, DAITO, CHIKUBU, IKUNA, SHISAKA, SAKITO. Traced from its profile (threshold 205, --open 3 to drop the derrick boom and stays) and scaled to the printed length (the 0-90 scale agrees to 1%); the topmasts, lost in the opening, drawn back as masts at the plate's positions and heights (scale: foremast 85', mainmast 65')

kaibokan1.name: KAIBOKAN No. 1 class PF (Type C kaibokan, odd numbers)
kaibokan1.plate: ONI 222-J, issued June 1945, p. 111 (scan leaf 134): length 220' 0" (oa), beam 28' 0", draft 11' 0"; 0-60 ft scale, dotted line at about 37'. Odd-numbered units (Nos. 1-53 listed); "formerly called PF-UN-2 class". Traced from its profile (threshold 205) and scaled to the printed length; the scale reads the mast top about 52', the trace 54'

kaibokan2.name: KAIBOKAN No. 2 class PF (Type D kaibokan, even numbers)
kaibokan2.plate: ONI 222-J, issued June 1945, p. 117 (scan leaf 140): length 260' 0" (oa), beam 31' 0", draft not printed; maximum speed 24 kts (est.), steam driven; 0-60 ft scale, dotted line at about 37'. Even-numbered units (Nos. 2-56, 112, 130 listed); "formerly called PF-UN-1 class". Traced from its profile (threshold 205) and scaled to the printed length; the scale reads the mast top about 55', the trace 57'

kamikaze.name: KAMIKAZE class DD
kamikaze.plate: ONI 222-J, issued June 1945, p. 51 (scan leaf 74): length 336' 6" (oa), 332' 0" (wl), beam 30' 0", draft 9' 7" (mean); 0-75 ft scale, dotted line at about 59'. Lists KAMIKAZE, HARUKAZE, HATAKAZE. Traced from its profile (threshold 205) and scaled to the printed length; the scale reads the foremast top about 69', the trace 72'

wakatake.name: KURI-WAKATAKE class ODD (MOMI and WAKATAKE classes)
wakatake.plate: ONI 222-J, issued June 1945, p. 69 (scan leaf 92): length 287' 0" (oa), 282' 0" (wl), beam 26' 6", draft 8' 3" (mean); 0-75 ft scale, dotted line at about 57'. Lists KURI, KAKI, TSUGA, HASU, ASAGAO; the plate draws the two classes as one. The upper of its two profiles (the lower is a DM conversion, est. 292' oa). The plate is a 1-bit stippled scan: blurred (2.5 px) before tracing at threshold 225 so the stipple reads as solid; scaled to the printed length; the scale reads the foremast top about 67', the trace 70' (the blur adds about 1'). The mainmast's topmast, detached on the plate, is dropped

chidori.name: CHIDORI class TB
chidori.plate: ONI 222-J, issued June 1945, p. 73 (scan leaf 96): length 268' 6" (oa), 253' 11" (wl), beam 24' 2", draft 6' 0" (mean); 0-60 ft scale, dotted line at about 47'. Lists CHIDORI, TOMOZURU, HATSUKARI (MANAZURU not listed). Foremast with ladder-type radar. Traced from its profile (threshold 205) and scaled to the printed length; the scale reads the foremast top about 54', the trace 56.5'

shirataka.name: SHIRATAKA (CM-3)
shirataka.plate: ONI 41-42, Japanese Naval Vessels, SHIRATAKA plate, Division of Naval Intelligence, June 1943 (scan leaf 242): length 259' 10" (wl), beam 37' 9", draft 9' 2" (normal); displacement 1,345 tons (standard); height lines at 15, 30, 45, 60 and 70 ft; *profile shows the new mounts, photos the old. The plate prints no overall length: the outline is traced (threshold 225, wires and masts dropped) and measured on the plate's own waterline bracket (259' 10" over 1,183 px), which the height lines confirm (4.57 px/ft); overall 279'. Masts drawn back at the plate's positions and heights (foremast to the 70 ft line)

type-tl-tanker.name: Type TL (Modified) tanker (Japanese wartime standard large tanker)
type-tl-tanker.plate: ONI 208-J Supplement 3, Standard Classes of Japanese Merchant Ships, p. 11 ("TYPE TL (Modified)", 54-MMF, Sugar Able Love; summary p. 3). Printed: 10,000 GT, 14,500 tons loaded, length o.a. 517', beam 67', draft loaded 29.7'; no heights. Traced from the profile and measured on the plate's scale bar (read as 100 ft), 515 ft. The plate's list for Types TL and TL (Modified) includes MIRII MARU, 10,564 GT (Miri Maru, HI-67). Type TL itself has no drawing ("design unknown"), so this is TL (Modified) standing for both. Mirrored to put the bow on the right

type-k-ore-carrier.name: Type K ore carrier (Japanese wartime standard, engines amidships)
type-k-ore-carrier.plate: ONI 208-J Supplement 3, Standard Classes of Japanese Merchant Ships, p. 10 ("TYPE K Ore Carrier", 23-MKFKM, Fox Tare Charlie; summary p. 3). Printed: 5,300 GT, 7,900 tons loaded, length o.a. 410', beam 59', draft loaded 24.5'; no heights. Traced from the profile and measured on the plate's scale bar (read as 100 ft), 403 ft. A typical engine-amidships ore carrier of the TE-04 kind: none of Kinrei, Toyohi, Daibu or Taiyoku Maru is in its list (or found anywhere in ONI 208-J). Mirrored to put the bow on the right

tokiwasan-maru.name: TOKIWASAN MARU, TAIHOSAN MARU (coastal freighters)
tokiwasan-maru.plate: ONI 208-J (Revised), Japanese Merchant Ships Recognition Manual (Jan 1945), p. 149 (24 MFM, "Taihosan Maru, Tokiwasan Maru", 1937, 1,805 GT, 2,420 DWT). Printed: W.L. (B.P.) 265', beam 38', drafts 18' loaded, 8'6" light; heights above the deck (the manual's "two constant points", explained in its front matter, scan ONI208J-p023): foremast 68', derrick heads 40', bridge 28', stack 40'. Measured on the scale bar (read as 100 ft): 278 ft overall; on the trace the foremast truck and derrick head stand about 69' and 39' above the forward well deck (checked by eye on the scan, not computed for the bridge and stack). Mirrored to put the bow on the right

type-d-mod.name: Type D (Modified) freighter (Japanese wartime standard, engines aft)
type-d-mod.plate: ONI 208-J Supplement 3, Standard Classes of Japanese Merchant Ships, p. 8 ("TYPE D (Modified)", 47-MKF, Sugar Charlie Love; summary p. 3). Printed: 2,300 GT, 3,870 tons loaded, length o.a. 310'-315', beam 49', draft loaded 19.2'; no heights. Traced from the profile and measured on the plate's scale bar (read as 100 ft), 312 ft. The plate's list for Types D and D (Modified) includes SHORYU MARU, 1,916 GT. The forward mast is drawn thick on the plate (derrick heels) and is kept as traced. Mirrored to put the bow on the right

type-tm-tanker.name: Type TM tanker (Japanese wartime standard medium tanker)
type-tm-tanker.plate: ONI 208-J Supplement 3, Standard Classes of Japanese Merchant Ships, p. 12 ("TYPE TM", 55-MMF, Sugar Able Item; Internet Archive leaf 0015). Printed: 5,200 GT, 7,000 tons loaded, length o.a. 410', beam 59', draft loaded 24'; no heights. "Approximately 40 had been built by 1 July 1944"; its list includes OTORISAN MARU 5,280 and SARAWAK MARU 5,135. Traced from the profile (threshold 200, closed 5 px, opened 5 px; the forestay erased first so the triangle under it stays open), measured on the plate's scale bar (four divisions, read as 100 ft, as for the other Supplement 3 plates: an inference), 410 ft, the printed length. Masts added back at the plate's positions: foremast truck about 97 ft and mainmast about 89 ft above the keel line as drawn (measured, not printed). The plate's dashed vertical line between the masts (a fitting not always present, inferred) is left out. Mirrored to put the bow on the right

no13-minesweeper.name: No. 13 class AM (minesweepers Nos. 13-18)
no13-minesweeper.plate: ONI 41-42, Japanese Naval Vessels, NO. 13 CLASS-AM 7-12 plate, Division of Naval Intelligence, June 1943 (scan leaf 253): length 236' 9" (oa), 232' 3" (wl) (Nos. 17, 18: 218' oa), beam 25', draft 6' 1" (normal); displacement 492-511 tons (standard); 2-4.7, 2-AAMG, mines; height lines at 15, 30, 45 and 60 ft. "6-No. 13 class". Traced from the profile (threshold 215, closed 3 px, opened 2 px; the lattice masts kept as traced) and scaled to the printed length overall: 10.13 px/ft against 10.3 px/ft from the plate's height lines, within 2%. Bow already to the right
